subject: general
question: In March 2025, the Indian Government has introduced a ______ incentive scheme for banks to encourage small-value UPI transactions in the financial year 2024-25?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**₹1,500 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Government introduced a **₹1,500 crore incentive scheme** in **March 2025** to encourage **small-value UPI transactions** during the financial year 2024-25.
 
• The primary aim of this initiative is to boost the adoption and usage of **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)**, particularly for **micro and small transactions**.
 
• This incentive is part of the government's effort to accelerate **digital payments** and reduce reliance on cash-based transactions.
 
• UPI has become one of the most popular and widely used payment systems in India, significantly contributing to **financial inclusion**.
 
• The scheme reflects the government's commitment towards promoting a **cashless economy** and leveraging **technology-driven financial solutions**.
 
• Such initiatives encourage banks to focus on increasing the penetration of UPI, especially in **rural and semi-urban areas** where digital payment adoption is comparatively lower.
 
• This move aligns with India's vision of becoming a global leader in **digital payments infrastructure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **₹1,700 crore**__

 __
 
• The incentive amount of **₹1,700 crore** might represent a higher allocation, but it is not the correct figure for the scheme introduced in March 2025.
 
• Higher allocations could indicate a more expansive effort towards promoting UPI transactions in future years.
 
 
 
• **₹1,800 crore**__
 __
 
• ₹1,800 crore as an option may reflect government policies or schemes with larger budgets, but it does not correspond to the **specific scheme for small-value UPI transactions** in FY 2024-25.
 
 
 
• **₹1,600 crore**__
 
 
• The allocation of **₹1,600 crore** could have been used for other financial or digital initiatives by the government, but it is not related to the **scheme introduced in March 2025**.
